passage: I'm Sharmila. At lunch today Minakshi wrinkled her nose when I opened my tiffin. It was methi paratha. My cheeks went hot and I shut the lid. I thought, she thinks my food is yucky. I stopped eating. Minakshi noticed and asked, “Did I do something?” I said, “You made a face at my lunch.” She looked around and laughed. “No! Someone at the next bench opened a boiled egg and it smells so strong!” I hadn't even noticed. She said, “Your paratha smells lovely, can I try a bit?”

qa.q: How did Sharmila feel when Minakshi wrinkled her nose, and what did she think it meant?
qa.a: She felt hurt and embarrassed, since her cheeks went hot and she shut the lid, thinking Minakshi found her food yucky. She had not noticed the smell from the next bench.
She asked, “Did I do something?” which let Sharmila say what she saw and let Minakshi explain the real reason.

qa.q: How might Minakshi have felt when she learned Sharmila thought it was about the paratha?
qa.a: Probably surprised and a bit sorry that her face had caused hurt. Her offer to try a bit shows she wanted to make it right.

grounding: A child sees a friend wrinkle her nose at lunch and feels hurt, but asking shows it was another smell.

passage: Note from Bidisha, class teacher. At lunch, Lakshmi's friend wrinkled her nose while Lakshmi was unpacking her tiffin. Lakshmi shut the box and stopped eating. I sat beside her and asked quietly what was wrong. She said, “She thinks my food smells.” I asked the friend, gently, what the face was about. She said the bin near their bench smelled sour. Lakshmi opened the box again. I suggested to them that when a face worries you, you can ask, “Was that about my food?” They tried the sentence together.

qa.q: What did Lakshmi do after her friend wrinkled her nose?
qa.a: She shut the box and stopped eating.

qa.q: What was Lakshmi probably feeling when she shut her tiffin, and what else could the friend's face have meant?
qa.a: Probably hurt and self-conscious, thinking her food was being rejected. The friend's face was actually about the sour smell from the bin.

qa.q: What small step did Bidisha suggest for next time?
qa.a: That when a face worries them, they ask something like “Was that about my food?” instead of assuming, and she had them practise it together.

qa.q: How might the friend have felt on learning Lakshmi had been hurt?
qa.a: Probably surprised and sorry, since she did not mean anything by it. She joined in practising the question, which suggests she wanted to make it right.

grounding: A child feels hurt by a wrinkled nose at her lunch; asking kindly avoids assuming rejection.
